newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco's El Teniente starts building acid plant.
newsitem.headline: Codelco's El Teniente starts building acid plant.

text.p: El Teniente division of Chile's state copper company Codelco will this week start building a $72 million sulphuric acid plant as part of a clean-up plan at its dirty Caletones smelter.
The plant, which will start operating in 1998, is the first of two El Teniente will build to reduce emissions of sulphur dioxide and other gases from the smelter.
"With these plants we will be able to meet all environment standards required by the industry toward 2003," said general manager Fernando Riveri in a statement.
Under the division's clean-up program, Caletones' sulphur emissions must fall to 115,000 tonnes in 2002 from the current level of 375,000 tonnes.
El Teniente will hold a ceremony Thursday to start construction of the plant which will produce 1,500 tonnes of acid a day.
